questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code preserves at-least-once delivery when processing fails? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A poll returns three records for one partition and the second one's handling throws an exception. What does the consumer do?
choices: Commits offsets past the second record and continues with the third.
Commits nothing for the batch, seeks back to the last committed offset, pauses, and the three records are polled again.
Skips the failing record and commits the other two.
Stops the consumer permanently so an operator can intervene.

questions.prompt: The application crashes after handleBatch completes but before commitSync. What is the consequence on restart?
choices: Nothing is redelivered, because the work was completed.
Only the last record of the batch is redelivered.
The batch is redelivered to this or another group member, because the committed offset still points before it.
The consumer group's offsets reset to the latest position.

questions.prompt: Why is it important that nextOffsets commits `offset + 1` for the last record of each partition?
choices: Kafka rejects a commit equal to an already-delivered offset.
The committed offset is the position of the next record to read; committing the record's own offset would redeliver that record after a restart.
It is required so that the offsets of different partitions stay in sync.
It skips one record so the consumer never reprocesses a poison message.
